source.title: Two failure modes of deep transformers and how to avoid them: a unified theory of signal propagation at initialisation

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Analyzes and experimentally evaluates how Transformer initialization and residual strength relate to signal propagation and training, using language modeling and collapse measures rather than benchmark classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper’s CIFAR classification claim is not tested. Rows cover its own TinyStories training results that bear on initialization and residual connections. Other theoretical predictions and figure-only curves without a textual outcome are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study reports initialization and residual-strength effects in Transformers with skip connections and LayerNorm. V3 concerns depth degradation and its prevention in convolutional networks; V4 concerns initialization-dependent learning speed and trainable depth in plain networks. These Transformer results measure a related phenomenon outside those stated versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the principal initialization experiments. The authors conclude that their signal-propagation theory unifies rank and entropy collapse and predicts viable combinations of query/key initialization scale and skip strength. Their conclusion also emphasizes preliminary evidence that gain-controlled attention avoids these failures, with larger-scale evaluation left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops an analytical signal-propagation theory and evaluates Transformer masked-language-model training on TinyStories; it does not use the cited CIFAR classification recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Training outcomes vary with query/key initialization scale β, self-attention residual strength αSA, and learning rate. The paper also predicts different collapse timing for pre-LN and post-LN, but does not report a corresponding training-speed comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: At low query/key initialization variance, 60-layer BERT-style models train with skip strengths 1.5 or 2 but fail with strength 1; high-variance 12-layer models fail at all three tested strengths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformer trainability depends jointly on query/key initialization scale and residual strength: stronger skips can prevent rank-collapse failure but do not prevent high-variance entropy-collapse failure.

fits_no_version.finding: In one-layer Transformer experiments, small initial query/key weights allow effective learning, whereas large weights produce concentrated attention and ineffective training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Query/key initialization scale affects attention entropy and learning in residual Transformers on TinyStories.

fits_no_version.finding: Reducing learning rate from 5e-4 to 1e-4 partially mitigates attention entropy collapse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate can moderate initialization-induced attention entropy collapse in the tested Transformer setting.

record.problems: Experiments use TinyStories masked language modeling rather than classification benchmarks. The reported training outcomes are qualitative, with no numeric training-error values in the text. Some relevant results are described through figure captions and curves.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Theoretical signal-propagation calculations, cosine-similarity measurements, attention visualizations, and figure-only learning curves were not entered as training-outcome rows where the text did not give a separately attributable training result.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted or random labels.
Spurious local minima and the benefit of additional student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth in plain networks; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization; very deep plain convolutional networks.
Loss recovery, curvature changes and divergence relative to an initial stability limit, and full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The qualitative training outcomes are supported by the supplied text, but their original version links and verdicts overextend the claims' architectural scope. States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, not denials of the reported Transformer outcomes. The text inconsistently numbers Figure 1 panels; Appendix A.1 identifies the learning curves as panel (f).

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer comparisons, regularization, and training error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.

Plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, ImageNet/CIFAR-10 classification error, and direct shortcut-versus-no-shortcut depth comparisons. This paper studies Transformer residual strength and training loss on TinyStories.
Activation-matched initializations in plain feedforward/CNN models, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer CNNs.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature/sharpness, squared-loss wide networks, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization’s effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.
